scenarios.situation: You hold a foreign passport and the money is pay you earned working in China
scenarios.route: M1 bank conversion and wire (or M8 Wise, M9 RMB remittance)
scenarios.documents: Passport; PRC tax payment records covering the income; payroll or contract showing the amount
scenarios.prc_tax: Individual income tax on pay, 3%-45%; the bank asks for the tax voucher
scenarios.us_side: Exchange-rate gain above $200 on the conversion is reported as capital gain; FBAR and Form 8938 if thresholds are met

scenarios.situation: You were a PRC citizen, became a US citizen, and the money is from before you emigrated
scenarios.route: M3 emigrant property transfer, approved by SAFE
scenarios.documents: Application and form; identity documents; proof that the household registration was cancelled; proof of income source and title; tax certificate
scenarios.prc_tax: Depends on what the assets were (pay, sale of housing, business); a tax certificate is part of the file
scenarios.us_side: Same reporting rules; exchange-rate gain measured from the dollar value when each yuan was acquired

scenarios.situation: You inherited the money or assets from someone in China
scenarios.route: M4 inheritance transfer, approved by SAFE
scenarios.documents: Notarised proof of inheritance; the decedent's title documents; tax certificate; identity documents
scenarios.prc_tax: China levies no inheritance tax (Ministry of Finance statement, 2017); housing passing to heirs carries no individual income tax
scenarios.us_side: Form 3520 if bequests from a foreign estate exceed $100,000 in the year; late filing costs 5% a month up to 25%

scenarios.situation: The money is from selling housing you owned in China
scenarios.route: M5 sale-proceeds remittance through the bank
scenarios.documents: Registered sale contract and registration proof; tax voucher for the sale; ID
scenarios.prc_tax: Property-transfer income is taxed at a flat 20% rate; other taxes on the sale were not researched here
scenarios.us_side: Sale gain is computed in dollars for the US return; not researched further here

scenarios.situation: You brought foreign currency into China, exchanged it for yuan and did not spend it all
scenarios.route: M2 reconversion with the original exchange memo
scenarios.documents: Passport and the original exchange memo, within 24 months of the exchange
scenarios.prc_tax: No taxable category identified for exchanging your own money back
scenarios.us_side: Exchange-rate gain rule applies to the yuan held

scenarios.situation: The balance includes bank interest earned in China
scenarios.route: Not confirmed: whether a bank accepts interest statements as source documents was not found in a source
scenarios.prc_tax: Individual income tax on savings-deposit interest has been temporarily not levied since 9 October 2008

scenarios.situation: Relatives in China want to give you their own money
scenarios.route: They buy and remit foreign exchange under their own annual quota; your own money may not travel under their quota
scenarios.documents: Their resident ID; the purchase is recorded against their own USD 50,000 yearly total
scenarios.us_side: Form 3520 if gifts from nonresident aliens exceed $100,000 in the year

scenarios.situation: You cannot document where the money came from
scenarios.route: No bank route for large sums was found; only the small-amount channels M11-M14 work on ID alone

methods.name: Bank conversion and wire of documented China income
methods.who: Foreign-passport holders with lawful current-account yuan income earned in China
methods.limit: The documented after-tax amount; no fixed yearly cap in the rule
methods.cost: 10 Nov 2026: spread 0.21% plus CNY 216.85 to CNY 410 per wire at Bank of China, or CNY 146.84 to CNY 280 at Agricultural Bank of China
methods.time: One branch visit once documents are accepted; wire transit time not published
pros: The route the rule itself names for foreign individuals
Cheapest priced route found: 0.22% to 0.23% at $400,000
One wire can carry the whole documented amount
cons: Needs tax vouchers and source documents showing the amount
The bank decides whether the documents are enough
Intermediary-bank deductions are not published
steps: Collect your passport, PRC tax payment records for the income, and payroll or contract papers showing the amount.
Ask the branch which papers it accepts; it must check that the purchase matches a real, documented source.
Buy dollars at the bank's selling rate up to the documented after-tax amount.
Wire the dollars to your own US account. Bank of China charges 0.1% (min CNY 50, max CNY 260) plus CNY 150 cable.
Optional: pay USD 25 for full-amount arrival so intermediary banks do not deduct from the wire.
Keep the exchange memo, wire receipt and tax records, and note the dollar value and date for your US return.

methods.name: Convert back unused yuan that you originally exchanged from foreign currency
methods.who: Foreign-passport holders who exchanged foreign currency into yuan
methods.limit: The unused amount on the original exchange memo, within 24 months
methods.cost: The bank's selling rate; no separate fee found in a source
pros: Needs only passport and the original memo
No tax documents required by the rule
cons: Only covers yuan that came from your own foreign currency
The memo expires 24 months after the exchange
steps: Find the original exchange memo and check it is less than 24 months old.
Take passport and memo to the bank and convert back up to the unused amount.
Foreign currency that was remitted in and never converted can be sent back by the same route on ID alone.

methods.name: Emigrant property transfer
methods.who: People who moved from mainland China and obtained foreign permanent residence or citizenship, for assets owned before that
methods.limit: The approved amount; staged above CNY 200,000
methods.cost: Each stage is a wire priced like M1; approval fee not published
methods.time: Two years from the first remittance to the last, under Art. 6
pros: The route written for former PRC citizens with pre-emigration assets
Covers savings, sale proceeds and other lawful property in one application
cons: Requires proof that the household registration was cancelled
Requires SAFE approval and a tax certificate
Art. 6 releases half first, half of the rest after one year, the balance after two
steps: Confirm the assets were yours before you obtained the foreign status.
Gather the application and form, identity documents, proof of household-registration cancellation, proof of income source and title, and the tax certificate.
Apply once, for the whole amount, to the SAFE branch where your household was registered.
After approval the bank sells foreign exchange and remits in the stages set by Art. 6; a total of CNY 200,000 or less may go at once.
Price each stage as a separate wire.

methods.name: Inheritance transfer
methods.who: Foreign citizens who inherit property in China
methods.limit: The approved amount; one application per decedent
methods.cost: A wire priced like M1; approval fee not published
methods.time: Approval time not published; may be remitted in one or several payments
pros: May be remitted in a single payment after approval
China levies no inheritance tax per the 2017 Ministry of Finance statement
cons: Requires notarised inheritance documents and SAFE approval
Bequests above $100,000 in a year trigger US Form 3520
steps: Obtain notarised proof of inheritance and the decedent's title documents.
Turn the estate assets into yuan and obtain the tax certificate.
Apply once per decedent to the SAFE branch where the decedent's household was registered.
After approval the bank sells foreign exchange and remits in one or several payments.
File Form 3520 with your US return if the year's bequests from the foreign estate exceed $100,000.

methods.name: Remit proceeds from selling housing in China
methods.who: Overseas individuals who sell housing they own in China
methods.limit: Sale price minus the taxes of that sale, and no more than the tax certificate shows
pros: Handled at the bank against a fixed list of papers
The cap is the after-tax sale amount, not a yearly quota
cons: Title transfer must already be registered
The bank refuses any amount above the tax certificate
steps: Complete the sale and register the title transfer.
Pay the taxes on the sale and obtain the tax voucher.
Bring ID, the registered sale contract, registration proof and tax voucher to the bank.
The bank checks the amount against the tax certificate, sells foreign exchange and remits.

methods.name: USD 50,000 yearly purchase quota
methods.who: Domestic individuals, and overseas individuals holding a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card. A US-passport holder without that card is not covered.
methods.limit: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per calendar year
methods.cost: A wire priced like M1 for each year's purchase
pros: ID only within the quota
No source documents within the quota
cons: Not open to ordinary foreign-passport holders
$400,000 takes eight calendar years
Splitting or borrowing quotas puts you on the watch list
steps: Check that you hold a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card.
Buy up to USD 50,000 equivalent in the calendar year on that ID.
Wire the dollars to your own account abroad.
Repeat in the next calendar year.

methods.name: HSBC China wire (Premier, Advance or Private Banking)
methods.who: HSBC China customers who meet the same documentary rules as M1
methods.cost: Premier and Advance: 0.1% (min CNY 100, max CNY 500) plus CNY 120 cable. Private Banking individuals: free. HSBC's exchange rate was not retrieved.
pros: Private Banking individuals pay no wire or cable fee
Pay Exact option for CNY 200
cons: Higher fee cap than Bank of China or Agricultural Bank of China
Premier needs CNY 500,000 total balance or the monthly fee
Spread unknown here
steps: Meet the same documentary rules as M1.
Convert at HSBC's own rate, then issue a telegraphic transfer.
Optional: Pay Exact for CNY 200 so the beneficiary receives the full dollar amount.

methods.name: Wise, sending from yuan
methods.who: People who are not mainland Chinese, who work or worked in China and hold a PRC tax record paid within the last three years
methods.limit: CNY 300,000 per transfer from a bank app, CNY 50,000 from Alipay; overall limit equals after-tax salary evidenced
methods.cost: Not published on the page; shown when a transfer is set up
pros: Done from a phone
Limit does not expire until used
cons: Only to an account you own
Tax records older than three years are not counted
$400,000 needs at least nine transfers
steps: Check that you meet the three conditions.
Start a transfer and upload tax records when asked.
Pay Wise by bank transfer from your China bank app or from Alipay.
Receive the money in your own account abroad.

methods.name: Send yuan abroad as yuan, convert offshore
methods.who: Individuals with employee pay, social benefits or family-support remittances, where a bank offers personal cross-border yuan settlement
methods.cost: Not published; the offshore conversion rate was not retrieved
pros: Policy covers employee pay since January 2018
Lets you choose where and when to convert
cons: Few US accounts can receive yuan
Fees and offshore rate unknown here
steps: Ask your bank whether it offers personal cross-border yuan remittance for pay.
Provide the same evidence of lawful income.
Convert offshore at the receiving bank's rate.

methods.name: Western Union through an agent bank
methods.who: Customers of an agent bank such as Postal Savings Bank of China
methods.limit: USD 10,000 per transaction at the counter, USD 5,000 online or mobile
methods.cost: Western Union's own fee, not published by the bank
pros: Cash pick-up abroad
The agent bank adds no fee of its own
cons: Small per-transaction limit
Fee not published
$400,000 needs at least 40 counter transactions
steps: Take your ID and account to an agent-bank counter or use its app.
Send dollars and note the tracking number.
Tell the recipient the details needed for pick-up.

methods.name: Withdraw cash abroad on a mainland bank card
methods.who: Any holder of a mainland bank card
methods.limit: CNY 10,000 per card per day; CNY 100,000 per person per calendar year across all cards
methods.cost: Bank of China: CNY 12 plus 1% per withdrawal, max CNY 112; the card network's rate and the ATM owner's surcharge are not published here
methods.time: $400,000 takes 27 calendar years at the yearly cap
pros: Needs no documents
Works from any overseas ATM that accepts the card
cons: About $15,000 a year
Exceeding the cap suspends overseas withdrawals for that year and the next
Fee above 1% before the network rate
steps: Use the card at an overseas ATM, at most CNY 10,000 a day per card.
Stop at CNY 100,000 for the calendar year across all your cards.
Deposit the cash in your US account.

methods.name: Carry dollar banknotes out of China
methods.who: Any traveller; buying the dollars still follows the purchase rules
methods.limit: USD 5,000 per trip with no permit; USD 5,000-10,000 with a bank permit; above USD 10,000 not allowed in principle
methods.cost: The bank's selling rate; permit CNY 10, waived until 31 December 2026 at Bank of China; travel cost not included
pros: No wire fee
No intermediary bank
cons: Theft and loss risk
Capped per trip
More than $10,000 must be reported on FinCEN Form 105 when entering the US
steps: Buy or withdraw dollar notes at the bank.
Carry up to USD 5,000 per trip, or up to USD 10,000 with a carrying permit from the bank.
File FinCEN Form 105 if you ever carry more than $10,000 into the US.

methods.name: Carry yuan banknotes out and exchange abroad
pros: No documents
No conversion in China
cons: Tiny capacity
Unknown rate abroad
steps: Carry at most CNY 20,000 per trip.
Exchange at a bank or bureau abroad.

methods.name: Passport-only small conversions
methods.who: Overseas individuals converting unused yuan back
methods.limit: USD 500 a day at a bank; USD 1,000 a day at airside counters before departure
methods.cost: The counter's selling rate; not retrieved for airside counters
methods.time: $400,000 takes 800 days at USD 500 a day
pros: Passport only
No memo needed
cons: Tiny capacity
Written for leftover exchanged yuan, not for savings
steps: Show your passport at the bank and convert up to USD 500 that day.
Before departure, convert up to USD 1,000 at an airside counter.

methods.name: Splitting the money across relatives' or friends' quotas
methods.who: Listed so you can recognise it. No steps are given.
methods.cost: Watch list for the current year and the next two; fines up to 30% of the amount, or 30% to 100% in serious cases
cons: Rule: individuals may not split transactions to evade the quota
Borrowers are listed; lenders get a warning and are listed if they repeat

methods.name: Underground banks, matched onshore-offshore swaps, private currency trades
methods.who: Listed so you can recognise it. No steps are given.
methods.cost: Warning, confiscation and fines up to 30%, or 30% to 100% in serious cases; a crime from CNY 5 million of turnover or CNY 100,000 of gains
cons: Art. 45 covers private and disguised buying and selling of foreign exchange
Counterparty can simply keep the money

methods.name: Buying crypto or stablecoins with yuan and selling abroad
methods.who: Listed so you can recognise it. No steps are given.
methods.cost: Exchange of legal tender for virtual currency is prohibited in China; contracts may be void and losses fall on you
cons: Banks and payment firms may not move money for it
The February 2026 notice replaced the 2021 one

methods.name: False contracts, invoices or other papers shown to the bank
methods.who: Listed so you can recognise it. No steps are given.
methods.cost: Ordered to convert back; fines up to 30%, or 30% to 100% in serious cases; criminal liability where a crime
cons: Art. 40 names false or invalid documents used to obtain foreign exchange

methods.name: Using an old PRC resident ID after becoming a US citizen
methods.who: Listed so you can recognise it. No steps are given.
methods.cost: Consequence not found in a source read here
cons: Chinese nationality is lost automatically on acquiring foreign nationality while settled abroad, and the ID should be cancelled
Banks classify the account by the ID shown; the domestic quota belongs to domestic individuals

penalty_layers.amount: 0.21% at Bank of China and Agricultural Bank of China, 0.22% at China Merchants Bank, 0.26% at ICBC, measured from each bank's own buy/sell midpoint on 10 Nov 2026

penalty_layers.layer: Wire handling fee and cable fee
penalty_layers.amount: Bank of China CNY 200-410 per wire; Agricultural Bank of China CNY 100-280; HSBC China Premier or Advance CNY 220-620
Not published. Avoidable for USD 25 at Bank of China (full-amount arrival) or CNY 200 at HSBC China (Pay Exact)
$15 at Chase and Bank of America; no fee at Schwab and Fidelity

penalty_layers.layer: PRC tax on the income behind the money
penalty_layers.amount: Pay 3%-45%; property-transfer income 20%; savings interest not levied since 2008; no inheritance tax. The transfer itself is not one of the nine taxable categories
A gain above $200 on a personal foreign-currency transaction is reported as capital gain. At 6.6851 the gain is 7.01% of the dollars received if the yuan was acquired at the 2024 average rate
FBAR: up to $16,536 non-willful, $165,353 willful. Form 8938: $10,000 plus up to $50,000. Form 3520: 5% a month up to 25%
Fines up to 30% of the amount, or 30% to 100% in serious cases; watch list for three calendar years; a crime from CNY 5 million of turnover
Emigrant transfers above CNY 200,000 take two years from the first remittance; the ATM cap is CNY 100,000 a year

other_banks.fee_note: National tariff for an ordinary wire not retrieved. One branch page lists ICBC Express relay at 0.1%, min CNY 50, max CNY 260, no cable fee
FAQ text: 0.1%, min CNY 100, cable CNY 100-150; no maximum in the text retrieved
2016 page: 0.1%, min CNY 20, max CNY 300, cable CNY 80; current tariff and rate board not retrieved
2017 notice gives ranges: counter 0.06%-0.1%, min CNY 20-50, max CNY 250; rate board not retrieved

claims.claim: USD 50,000 annual quota
claims.finding: The quota covers FX purchases by domestic individuals. An overseas individual gets it only with a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card.

claims.claim: PRC individual income tax 3%-45% on pay; flat 20% on interest, dividends, property transfer
claims.finding: Matches Art. 3 of the law.

claims.claim: HSBC China wire: 0.1%, min CNY 100, max CNY 500, plus CNY 120 cable; a $400,000 wire costs CNY 620
claims.finding: Matches items 2.2.4.1 and 2.2.4.2 of the tariff effective 31 Oct 2026 for Premier and Advance. Private Banking individuals are free.

claims.claim: CNY 620 is about $86.97
claims.finding: That figure divides by 7.129, the IRS 2025 yearly average. At the Bank of China selling rate of 10 Nov 2026 (6.6851) CNY 620 is $92.74.

claims.claim: HSBC Premier needs a total balance of CNY 500,000
claims.finding: Important Notes 3(1) of the tariff.

claims.claim: HSBC Global Transfer: free for Private Banking and Premier, USD 20 for Advance
claims.finding: The Global Transfer rows of the tariff were not read by this session.

claims.claim: A personal foreign-currency gain is not income unless it exceeds $200; above that, capital gain
claims.finding: Matches Publication 525 and 26 U.S.C. 988(e)(2). No page in the repository puts a dollar figure on the gain; this site does.

claims.claim: FBAR penalties $16,536 non-willful and $165,353 willful
claims.finding: Matches the eCFR table for penalties assessed on or after 17 January 2025. The '50% of the balance' alternative was not re-read here.

claims.claim: Form 8938 penalty $10,000 plus continuing penalties up to $60,000 in total
claims.finding: IRS: $10,000 plus up to $50,000 more. Joint-filer thresholds were not re-read here.

claims.claim: PRC fines up to 30% of the amount, or 30% to 100% in serious cases
claims.finding: Matches Arts. 39, 40 and 45 of Decree 532.

claims.claim: Overseas ATM cap CNY 100,000 per person per year
claims.finding: Plus CNY 10,000 per card per day, and a suspension for that year and the next if exceeded.

claims.claim: USD 5,000 in cash per trip without a permit
claims.finding: USD 5,000-10,000 needs a bank permit; above USD 10,000 is not allowed in principle.

claims.claim: Wise: at most CNY 300,000 per bank-app transfer
claims.finding: Also: own account only, and tax records paid within the last three years.

claims.claim: Emigrant or inheritance transfer: lump sum OK after approval
claims.finding: True for inheritance. For emigrant transfers above CNY 200,000, Art. 6 requires three stages over two years. ladder/data/sources.json:64 states the staging correctly, so the repository contradicts itself.

claims.claim: A foreigner resident in China for a year is a 'domestic individual' (Decree 532 Art. 52)
claims.finding: The article says so. The Individual FX Measures instead classify by the ID document held, and SAFE Tianjin ties the quota to the Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card.

claims.claim: Yin Fa [2026] No. 42 bans exchanging yuan for virtual currency
claims.finding: It also repeals Yin Fa [2021] No. 237, which ladder/data/sources.json:207 still lists as a source.

claims.claim: Unused yuan can be converted back: USD 500 a day on passport alone, memo valid 24 months
claims.finding: The rule is about yuan originally exchanged from foreign currency, not savings in general.

claims.claim: The FX spread cannot be verified, so every all-in cost is blank
claims.finding: Four banks publish buy and sell rates. This session read them on 10 Nov 2026 and computed the spread for each.

claims.claim: IRS 2025 yearly average rate for China is 7.129
claims.finding: It is a yearly average for tax reporting, not a rate at which a bank converts.

claims.claim: Cost tables price HSBC China only
claims.finding: Before this session no page cited another mainland bank's tariff. Bank of China and Agricultural Bank of China publish lower caps: CNY 410 and CNY 280 per wire against CNY 620.

flags.item: Intermediary-bank deductions on a standard wire
flags.why: No bank publishes them. Left blank; the published alternative is USD 25 full-amount arrival at Bank of China.

flags.item: HSBC China exchange rate and spread
flags.why: HSBC's rate board was not retrieved. Its fee is converted to dollars at the PBOC central parity, which is an approximation.

flags.item: ICBC fee for an ordinary cross-border wire
flags.why: The national page gives no figure; only one branch page was found. Left blank in the ladder.

flags.item: China Merchants Bank wire fee
flags.why: The text retrieved gives no maximum and a cable range of CNY 100-150. Left blank.

flags.item: China Construction Bank wire fee
flags.why: The only official text found is dated 2016. Left blank.

flags.item: Bank of Communications wire fee
flags.why: The 2017 notice gives ranges, not single figures. Left blank.

flags.item: Wise fee for sending from yuan
flags.why: The help page states no fee. Left blank.

flags.item: Western Union fee from China
flags.why: The agent bank says the fee is Western Union's own and does not publish it. Left blank.

flags.item: Card-network exchange rate and ATM-owner surcharge
flags.why: Not retrieved. The ATM ladder shows the issuing bank's fee only.

flags.item: Cost of sending yuan abroad as yuan
flags.why: No fee or offshore rate was retrieved. Left blank.

flags.item: Whether emigrant transfers are still staged
flags.why: Art. 6 of the 2004 rule stages them and is the text on SAFE's site. Whether a later rule relaxed this was not established. Plan for staging and ask the approving SAFE branch.

flags.item: Who counts as a 'domestic individual'
flags.why: Decree 532 Art. 52 includes foreigners resident for one year; the Individual FX Measures classify by ID document. The effect on a long-resident foreigner's quota was not established.

flags.item: FBAR filing threshold, the 50%-of-balance willful alternative, and joint Form 8938 thresholds
flags.why: Not re-read by this session. Left blank here.

flags.item: How the $200 rule and holding periods apply to a pooled deposit
flags.why: Whether each conversion is one transaction, and which yuan are treated as converted first, was not found in a source. Needs a tax professional.

flags.item: Age of the Bank of China fee tables
flags.why: The price-list PDF is dated 31 March 2025 and the web table 2014. The 2025 mobile-banking discount ended 31 December 2025 and no later notice was found, so no discount is applied.

flags.item: Exchange rates are a snapshot
flags.why: Boards were read between 17:39 and 17:51 Beijing time on 10 Nov 2026. The live rate at the time of your transaction governs.

flags.item: Sources read only as search excerpts
flags.why: 37 of 53 sources are text the search index returned for an official URL; the page body was not opened. Each is marked 'excerpt' on the Sources page.

flags.item: HSBC tariff document
flags.why: The PDF effective 31 Oct 2026 carries a stray page header dated 12 September 2024. The Global Transfer rows were not read.

flags.item: PRC taxes on a housing sale other than the 20% rate
flags.why: Value-added tax, deed tax and local practice were not researched. Left blank.

flags.item: Inheritance-tax statement is from 2017
flags.why: No later official statement was retrieved.

flags.item: US tax on interest earned on the account, foreign tax credit, foreign earned income exclusion
flags.why: Not researched by this session. Left blank.

flags.item: Rate used to turn the wire amount into yuan for the 0.1% fee
flags.why: The tariff does not say. This site uses the bank's own selling rate; the effect is under CNY 1 per wire.

flags.item: Your own facts
flags.why: Source of the money, the ID used to open the account, the bank, and the dates the yuan was acquired are unknown. No personal tax amount or eligibility is asserted.
